decisions.reason: The message's separate footer-code correction is already fully represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY; the report-detail identifier change requires no additional footer-state change.
The message's separate internal-header correction is already fully represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY; the report-detail identifier change requires no additional header-state change.

The exposure-level corrections in the source message are already represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY, while correcting RR03 and RR04 report-detail identifiers does not change the variant set.
Correcting report-detail identifiers does not alter the required risk-appropriate customer-facing copy.
The internal-page header's coverage, style, and information requirements remain unchanged; exact per-variant header codes are owned by the separate header-code consistency Requirement.
The report-detail identifier correction does not change the premium visual-design standard, design direction, or cross-variant visual consistency.
Although the corrected report details appear on page 1, the decision does not change the dashboard's fields, prominence, heading, or visibility requirements.
The RR03 and RR04 report-detail identifier correction does not affect the content or scannable presentation of the front-page result explanation.
Assigning the correct report IDs to RR03 and RR04 does not change the requirement that report-ID and other customer-specific fields remain editable.
The generic footer structure, coverage, and warning coexistence requirements remain unchanged; exact variant footer codes are handled by the separate footer-code consistency Requirement.
Correcting report-detail identifiers has no necessary effect on the final-page distribution warning's presence, message, visual treatment, or footer relationship.
The report-detail identifier correction does not change how the vehicle group must be presented.
